layers.note: A spring ephemeral of meadows, open woods and grassland, flowering at snowmelt; abundant in wet mountain meadows (FEIS, Fryer 2021).

moisture.note: Moist in spring, drying in summer.

heat_load.note: Any aspect; follows the melting snow.

elevation_m.note: Sea level to alpine; 0 to 2,300 m in Oregon and to 3,675 m in Colorado (FEIS, Fryer 2021).

shade_tolerance.note: Sun to part shade; more flowers where conifers are sparse (FEIS, Fryer 2021).

coldest_c.note: Across its range, coldest-month means from about −15 to 4 °C; gone below −25 °C and above 8 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −38 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −45 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 9 to 22 °C; gone below 6 °C, where summers are too short, and above 26 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 800 to 4,500 degree-days above 0 °C, none below 500.

degree_days_5.note: About 250 to 2,800 degree-days above 5 °C, none below 100.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.3, gone by 0.15.

summer_rain.note: No lower limit: summer-dry Cascade summers suit it; up to about 0.55 of the year's precipitation in summer, gone by 0.75.

provenance.notes: Authored for the Mount Rainier subalpine meadow scene (Paradise, about 1,650 m) from general knowledge of the species; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Yellow avalanche-lily grows from southern British Columbia and Alberta south to northwestern California and northern New Mexico, abundant from Mt. Rainier to Mt. Hood (FEIS, Fryer 2021). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
